name: Montenegro
summary: A red field with a golden border and the coat of arms in the centre: a crowned golden double-headed eagle holding a sceptre and orb, with a lion on its breast. It was adopted in 2004, two years before independence from Serbia and Montenegro.
origin: The design is based on the royal standard of King Nikola I of Montenegro (r. 1860–1918), whose kingdom was absorbed into Yugoslavia in 1918.
Montenegro adopted the flag on 13 July 2004, Statehood Day, while still in a union with Serbia, and kept it after independence was declared in June 2006.

colors.name: Red

colors.name: Gold
colors.meaning: The border and the arms; royal heritage.

symbols.name: Double-headed eagle
symbols.description: A crowned golden eagle holding a sceptre and an orb.
symbols.meaning: From the Nemanjić and Crnojević traditions; Byzantine heritage and sovereignty.

symbols.name: Lion passant
symbols.description: A golden lion on a blue shield over green, on the eagle's breast.
symbols.meaning: The lion of Judah, a symbol of episcopal and royal authority in old Montenegro.

history.label: Socialist Republic of Montenegro

facts: It is one of the few national flags with a border all the way around.
Statehood Day, 13 July, marks recognition by the Congress of Berlin in 1878 and the 1941 uprising.
Albania's flag also shows a double-headed eagle on red, in black rather than gold.
clues: A gold-bordered red flag with a crowned golden double-headed eagle.
Its eagle has a lion on its breast.
Adopted two years before its country left a union in 2006.
